security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed skill files. The static findings are explained by Markdown examples, ordinary pymatgen imports, placeholder Materials Project API key guidance, expected local export files, and disclosed Materials Project network usage.

remediation.issue: API key setup examples mention persistent shell configuration files.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend scoped environment variables or a secret manager, and warn users not to paste real API keys into prompts.

remediation.issue: Bundled scripts can write output files selected by the user.
remediation.suggestion: Document that scripts should be run in a project directory and that chosen output paths may overwrite existing files.

remediation.issue: Materials Project workflows require external network access.
remediation.suggestion: State that phase diagram and database workflows contact Materials Project and may require account credentials.

content.value_statement: Materials researchers need reliable ways to inspect structures, convert formats, and interpret computed materials data. This skill provides pymatgen workflows, scripts, and references for those tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains pymatgen APIs for Structure, Lattice, Molecule, Composition, and transformations.
Converts CIF, POSCAR, XYZ, PDB, JSON, and YAML structure formats through documented scripts.
Analyzes symmetry, lattice parameters, coordination environments, density, and distance matrices.
Builds phase diagrams and stability reports using Materials Project entries.
Guides VASP, Gaussian, and Quantum ESPRESSO input generation with pymatgen helpers.
Provides references for band structures, density of states, surfaces, slabs, and workflows.
limitations: Requires a local Python environment with pymatgen and optional mp-api dependencies.
Materials Project workflows require the user to provide an API key and network access.
Does not run electronic structure simulations or guarantee calculation convergence.
Analysis quality depends on valid input structures and complete calculation output files.

use_cases.title: Inspect a New Crystal Structure
use_cases.description: Load a CIF or POSCAR file, summarize composition, symmetry, lattice parameters, and coordination environments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Computational Inputs
use_cases.description: Generate VASP or other code inputs from pymatgen structures using standard input sets and documented workflows.

use_cases.title: Screen Materials Stability
use_cases.description: Query Materials Project data, construct phase diagrams, and compare candidate compositions against the convex hull.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Structure File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pymatgen skill to convert my CIF structure to POSCAR. Explain the command, expected files, and how I can verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Structure Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this structure file with pymatgen. Report formula, space group, lattice parameters, density, and likely coordination environments.

prompt_templates.title: Check Phase Stability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pymatgen and Materials Project data to evaluate stability for LiFeO2 in the Li-Fe-O chemical system. Explain each assumption.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Screening Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pymatgen workflow to create doped structures, generate VASP inputs, track transformations, and summarize post-run stability data.

output_examples.input: Analyze a POSCAR file for symmetry, lattice parameters, and nearest neighbors.
output_examples.output: A concise structure report with reduced formula, space group, crystal system, lattice constants, density, site list, and coordination notes.

output_examples.input: Evaluate LiFeO2 stability from Materials Project entries.
output_examples.output: A phase stability summary listing stable competing phases, energy above hull, likely decomposition products, and interpretation of metastability.

output_examples.input: Prepare a band structure calculation workflow from a relaxed VASP structure.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step workflow covering relaxation review, static calculation setup, non-self-consistent band path generation, and band gap analysis.

best_practices: Use scoped Materials Project API keys and avoid pasting real secrets into prompts.
Validate input structures before converting formats or generating calculation inputs.
Cache Materials Project query results when repeating the same phase diagram analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a converted structure is correct without checking species, cell, and symmetry.
Do not run bundled scripts in directories where output files could overwrite important work.
Do not treat Materials Project results as a substitute for convergence checks in new calculations.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use pymatgen for structure analysis, format conversion, phase diagrams, electronic data, and workflow setup.

faq.question: Do I need a Materials Project API key?
faq.answer: Only workflows that query Materials Project need an API key. Local structure conversion and analysis do not need one.

faq.question: Can it convert CIF and POSCAR files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included guidance and converter script cover common structure formats, including CIF, POSCAR, XYZ, JSON, and YAML.

faq.question: Does it run VASP or other simulation engines?
faq.answer: No. It can help generate inputs and analyze outputs, but external simulation software must be run separately.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing results?
faq.answer: Check file formats, units, structure validity, convergence status, and whether any API-derived data should be cited.
